**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-03**
**Member: Emerson Iverson**
**Member ID: W898477218**
**Reference number: POC-007830134D-50943**
**Service denied: Lower back disc surgery / decompression, CPT 63030**
**Plan: Medicaid (Arkansas)**

---

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of the lower back disc surgery and decompression (CPT 63030) that my surgeon requested for me. The plan denied the prior authorization on 2026-08-03, stating in ordinary terms that the imaging findings submitted did not support medical necessity. I am asking the plan to reconsider that decision and to approve this surgery.

**The plan's own criteria have not been quoted to me.**

I want to be straightforward about one thing at the start. The denial notice says the decision was made under the plan's applicable medical policy and clinical review criteria, but the notice did not tell me the name of that policy, did not include the criteria, and did not explain which specific requirement my imaging was found not to meet. Because I have not been given that language, I am not quoting it anywhere in this letter, and I am not going to guess at what it says. I can only show the plan what is actually in my medical record, which I do below.

**Formal request for the criteria in writing.**

I am requesting, in writing, a copy of the clinical criteria applied to my prior authorization for CPT 63030 — the specific policy, guideline, or review vendor criteria the reviewer used, including any imaging requirement the reviewer believed my MRI did not satisfy. The plan holds these criteria; I do not. I am also requesting the name and specialty of the reviewer who made this determination. I am sending a copy of this request to the Arkansas Medicaid agency. Please send the criteria to me at the address above so that I have a fair opportunity to respond to the actual standard being applied to my care.

**What my records actually show.**

My surgeon, Dr. Duval, an orthopedic surgeon, has documented that this procedure is needed. The prior authorization packet contains the following:

- **Imaging.** An MRI of the lumbar spine on 2026-05-26 showed an L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root. This is a structural finding on imaging, at a specific level, with identified nerve root compression.
- **Symptoms that match the imaging.** I have had 18 months of progressive lower back pain that is not relieved by rest, with radicular pain going down into my right calf — the right side, matching the right-sided stenosis on the MRI.
- **Examination findings that match the imaging.** My exam showed positive provocative testing on the affected side and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level.
- **Conservative treatment, completed and documented.** I completed supervised physical therapy, including core stabilization and lumbar flexibility work, over 16 weeks from 2026-03-04 to 2026-06-24, with 16 visits completed. This is documented in the physical therapy discharge note. I took NSAIDs for 6 months with inadequate relief. I had a corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-04, which gave me only about 4 weeks of partial relief.
- **Functional impact.** I cannot stand for more than 10 minutes.
- **Surgical candidacy.** I have no active infection and no untreated substance use, my BMI is 29, and I am a non-smoker.

**Why I am asking for reconsideration.**

The stated basis for the denial is the imaging. My imaging is not equivocal or incidental. It identifies a disc extrusion, severe lateral recess stenosis, and compression of a specific nerve root — and my symptoms and my physical examination findings line up with that exact level and that exact side. Imaging findings, exam findings, and reported symptoms all point to the same place. I have also gone through months of non-surgical treatment first, and it is documented.

Since the plan has not told me what imaging threshold it applied, I cannot address it directly, and I would ask that the reviewer either identify the specific requirement my MRI was found not to meet or reconsider the determination on the complete record. If the plan maintains the denial, I ask that the response state precisely which criterion was not satisfied and quote it, so that I can respond to it.

**What I am asking for.**

I ask that the plan overturn the denial and authorize the lower back disc surgery and decompression (CPT 63030) requested by Dr. Duval. If additional records would help — the operative request, the physical therapy discharge note, the MRI report and images, or my office notes — please tell me specifically what is needed and I will arrange for it to be sent promptly.

My denial notice states that my appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of the notice, by **2027-01-30**, and I am submitting this letter within that period. I am sending it to the appeal address printed on my denial notice. I understand that, as an Arkansas Medicaid member, I may also request a state fair hearing, and I reserve that right. If any part of this appeal has been sent to the wrong department, I ask that you forward it to the correct one and let me know.

Thank you for taking the time to review my case again.

Sincerely,

**[Signature]**

Emerson Iverson
Member ID: W898477218
[My Phone Number]
[My Email Address, if I want to include one]

**Enclosures:** [List what I am attaching — e.g., copy of denial notice dated 2026-08-03; MRI lumbar spine report dated 2026-05-26; physical therapy discharge note; surgeon's office notes]

**cc:** Arkansas Medicaid agency [address as printed on my denial notice]
Dr. Duval, Orthopedic Surgery

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*

evidence.submission_route: Medicaid is run by your state. Appeal through your state Medicaid agency or your managed-care plan, and you can also ask for a state fair hearing. All of the details are on your denial letter. By phone: the number on the back of your insurance card Deadline: Often just 30 to 90 days — act quickly and check your letter -- but your denial letter is authoritative. Use the appeal address printed on your denial letter.
evidence.criteria_request: Most state Medicaid programs publish the rules for HOW a decision must be made but not the medical criteria for a specific surgery - those usually sit with your managed-care plan or its review vendor. Ask your plan in writing for 'the clinical criteria applied to my prior authorization', and copy your state Medicaid agency. Massachusetts, North Carolina and California are the exceptions - they publish real procedure criteria.
